review.alternative: Traditional reward-based modeling may be mathematically equivalent under restrictive assumptions.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical evidence demonstrating that non-reward oracle formulations fail to outperform standard Bradley-Terry reward models in standard tasks.

claims.statement: RLHF can be formulated under a general preference oracle without assuming a traditional reward function or Bradley-Terry model.

support.explanation: The authors explicitly define their framing around general preference oracles instead of traditional reward functions.
support.passage: In particular, we do not assume the existence of a reward function and an oracle preference signal drawn from the Bradley-Terry model as most of the prior works do.

actions.findings: RLHF can be formulated under a general preference oracle without assuming a traditional reward function or Bradley-Terry model. [source-a9ab68e18d3c4eb6]
actions.limitations: Empirical validation remains limited to specific algorithmic configurations; long-term longitudinal path dependence of preferences without explicit instruction has not been fully isolated.
actions.next_questions: How do preference oracles evolve over extended trajectories of multi-turn agent interaction?
actions.reason: Synthesizing collected literature on general preference oracles and RLHF formulations for project proj-emergent-prefs-01.
